scope: Generated Round79 diagnostic FP16 encoder candidate; never imported by production.

edits.purpose: The module docstring must not claim plain BF16 weights once the candidate also supports FP16.
Mark the module as the generated diagnostic candidate and pin the origin it was built from.
Add the dtype resolver and promote the vocabulary-embedding all-reduce to FP32 for FP16, matching the single-device reference sum; the BF16 branch keeps its existing gate.
Add the FP16 RMSNorm branch with the reference's two rounding points (FP32 reduction, cast to FP16, FP16 gamma multiply). The BF16 block is preserved verbatim.
Route FP16 text M-RoPE through the FP32-frequency branch so cos/sin are cast to FP16 exactly as the reference returns them; the BF16 gate is unchanged.
Use the reference's FP32 bilinear weights and FP32 four-term sum for both diagnostic dtypes instead of gating it behind VLLM_OMNI_910A_VISION_FP32.
Define compute_dtype before the early return so unloaded instances still expose it.
Replace the inline env parse with the single dtype resolver and record the resolved compute dtype plus the FP16-mode flag on the encoder.
Add the I/O dtype accessor and a fail-closed self-check so a mixed parameter dtype can never be silently benchmarked as one FP16 graph.
Take the image input dtype from the stored vision parameters instead of a hardcoded BF16 cast.
Same boundary fix for the video pixels.
Return the graph's own dtype. The reference has no final BF16 hop, so the hardcoded cast was an encoder-specific extra rounding. Hidden is already the compute dtype, so the BF16 result is unchanged.

notes: Regenerating from the pinned source reproduces the candidate byte for byte.
Every difference from the source lies inside a declared original_lines span.
TEXT_PAD_KV / TEXT_FP32_LINEAR / _text_fp32_local_linear do not exist in this R76 source; they belong to the separate round65 candidate and needed no disabling here.
BF16 branches are preserved verbatim; the interpolation edit intentionally moves BF16 to the reference-faithful FP32 form, so BF16-vs-production is not bit-identical.
